Activity.title: Activity
Activity.description: Represents a single activity option that users can select for their day plans, sourced from a curated list.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Activity entity.

name.description: The name or title of the activity.

description.description: A detailed description of the activity.

type.description: The category or type of activity (e.g., 'Historical Site', 'Dining', 'Nature').

address.description: The full street address of the activity's location.

latitude.description: The geographical latitude coordinate of the activity's location.

longitude.description: The geographical longitude coordinate of the activity's location.

estimatedDurationMinutes.description: The estimated duration in minutes typically required to experience this activity.

website.description: An optional URL for the activity's official website.

imageURL.description: An optional URL for an image representing the activity.

notes.description: Any additional notes or specific details about the activity.

sourceSpreadsheetRow.description: Optional reference to the original row number in the source spreadsheet/CSV for data tracing.

DayPlan.title: DayPlan
DayPlan.description: Represents a user-created daily itinerary, composed of a sequence of selected activities.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DayPlan entity.

name.description: A user-defined name for this day plan (e.g., 'Liz's First Day').

description.description: An optional longer description or notes for the entire day plan.

planDate.description: The specific date for which this day plan is created.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the day plan was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the day plan was last updated.

dayPlanActivityIds.description: An ordered list of references to DayPlanActivity entities that constitute this day plan. (Relationship: DayPlan 1:N DayPlanActivity)

DayPlanActivity.title: DayPlanActivity
DayPlanActivity.description: Represents a specific instance of an Activity included within a DayPlan, capturing its order, optionality, and planned timing.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DayPlanActivity entity.

dayPlanId.description: Reference to the DayPlan this activity belongs to. (Relationship: DayPlan 1:N DayPlanActivity)

activityId.description: Reference to the Activity being included in the plan. (Relationship: Activity 1:N DayPlanActivity)

sequenceNumber.description: The sequential order of this activity within its DayPlan, starting from 1.

startTime.description: An optional specific planned start time for this activity on the day.

endTime.description: An optional specific planned end time for this activity on the day.

isOptional.description: A flag indicating if this activity is optional for the day, meaning it might not be included in route calculations.

notes.description: Any specific notes related to this activity as part of the plan (e.g., 'check opening hours').

definition.description: Publicly accessible, curated list of activities. Read-only for authenticated users, with administrative write access for data ingestion.

params.name: activityId
params.description: Unique identifier for a specific activity.

definition.description: User-specific day plans. Each document's ownership is derived from the `{userId}` in the path, implicitly making `ownerId` equal to `userId` for security rules.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this day plan.

params.name: dayPlanId
params.description: Unique identifier for a specific day plan.

definition.description: Specific activities included within a user's day plan. This document includes denormalized `ownerId` (the user's UID) and `dayPlanId` for authorization independence, allowing security rules to validate access without reading parent documents.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the parent day plan.

params.name: dayPlanId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent day plan.

params.name: dayPlanActivityId
params.description: Unique identifier for a specific activity within a day plan.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation to ensure robust, debuggable, and scalable security rules.Activities, being a curated and global dataset, are placed in a top-level collection '/activities/{activityId}'. This collection has a homogeneous security posture: read-only for all authenticated users (and potentially unauthenticated ones, depending on requirements) and restricted write access for administrative functions (e.g., data ingestion). This separation ensures that global data does not interfere with user-specific authorization logic.

User-created DayPlans and their associated DayPlanActivities are strictly segregated under a user's private path: '/users/{userId}/dayPlans/{dayPlanId}' and '/users/{userId}/dayPlans/{dayPlanId}/dayPlanActivities/{dayPlanActivityId}'. This hierarchical structure directly implements Path-Based ownership, making `request.auth.uid == userId` the primary authorization check. This simplifies rules for both `DayPlan` and `DayPlanActivity` collections, as ownership is inherently defined by the path.

Crucially, for Authorization Independence, the `DayPlanActivity` entity denormalizes authorization context from its parent. Each `DayPlanActivity` document will include a `dayPlanId` field (referencing its parent `DayPlan`) and an `ownerId` field (referencing the `userId` from the path, which is `request.auth.uid`). This denormalization means that security rules for `DayPlanActivity` documents do not need to perform `get()` operations on the parent `DayPlan` document to ascertain ownership or access rights. This strategy eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies, enabling atomic operations and simplifying rule evaluation significantly.

This design effectively supports QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters) by ensuring that `list` operations can be secured efficiently. For instance, a user can only list `DayPlan`s within their own `/users/{request.auth.uid}/dayPlans` collection, and similarly for `DayPlanActivity` documents within their specific `DayPlan`. The denormalized `ownerId` and `dayPlanId` fields within `DayPlanActivity` allow for direct rule evaluation on the document itself, preventing unintended data leakage during `list` queries. Any future collaboration features would extend this model by denormalizing a 'members' map into the `DayPlan` (and subsequently into `DayPlanActivity` if needed for subcollection access) to maintain authorization independence.
